in

I'm a final-year PhD student at the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics & Max Planck School of Cognition in Tübingen, Germany, in the group of Prof. Peter Dayan. My interdisciplinary research lies at the intersection of computational cognitive science/neuroscience, human-centred AI and machine learning, where I study higher-order cognitive phenomena such as creativity, aesthetics, and design.

Highlights of my PhD:

  • Published 12 papers, including 7 as first author, across leading venues such as Nature, CogSci, ICLR, and NeurIPS.
  • Completed two industry internships at Toyota Research Institute and Bertelsmann SE & Co. KGaA, to gain practical experience translating research findings into real-world applications.
  • Parts of my work have been featured in news channels all over Germany.
  • Recipient of the Robert Francès Award for outstanding contributions to Empirical Aesthetics, and two Paper Awards.
  • Reviewed for top aesthetics and creativity journals and co-supervised two Masters students.

I am currently on the industry job market and wish to continue tackling hard problems at the frontier of human-centred AI and AI for creativity. Reach out at surabhi.s.nath@maxplanckschools.de for a chat.
